_read_this_first: These are tier claims KNOWN to be unevidenced. They are counted and printed on every run; they only withhold the exit code. The register is a RATCHET: an unevidenced claim that is NOT listed here fails the gate, and an entry whose debt is gone (claim now evidenced, or row deleted, or claim demoted) ALSO fails the gate. It can shrink; it cannot grow silently and it cannot outlive its reason.
_measured: 2026-08-08, ai_docs/2026-08-08-compat-envelope-baseline.md. Qualifying claims across the four scorecards: 6 before retirement, 0 after. Evidenced: 0 both times. The measured full-tier envelope is 0, and it is now 0 in the DATA rather than only in a checker.
_sequencing_rule: Do not expand envelope coverage until a qualifying tier can be earned honestly. Both qualifying tiers name stack and heap, which the schema cannot express (one hash per row, no reference operand); settling that is a reserved schema decision. Until it is settled no producer can emit a qualifying tier, so any new one would be refused by validate-envelope.sh.
_currently_empty_and_why: EMPTY is the correct state, not an unfilled stub. The six full-stdout-info-stack-heap claims registered here on 2026-08-08 were RETIRED the same day, because they had no producer in the tree: 'ptrace-short-full-tier' appeared only in docs, this register and the CSVs, and their commit ddfd448 changed only scorecard.csv with zero code. They could not be re-derived and no producer fix could re-emit them. They were demoted to legacy-unqualified by compat-envelope/retire_unevidenced_tier_claims.py -- a committed, idempotent tool, not by hand -- so nothing is owed here any more. The ratchet forced this prune: leaving the entries in place while the debt was gone failed the gate with 6 STALE.
_if_you_add_an_entry: Only for debt that genuinely exists and that you intend to clear. Every entry needs file, test_id, test_mode, backend, tier and a 'why' naming what would make it evidenced. An entry without a reason is refused at load.
